ΔE00 is the color difference from the input RGB image. The Magic check excludes density and antenna rules and is not a manufacturing sign-off.

For the two most-used cells of each case, we reran with 51 instead of 31 modes and a 0.5 nm instead of 1 nm step. The predicted color changed by at most ΔE00 = 0.311. This is not a convergence guarantee for every cell; see numerical_checks.json in each folder.

Each folder holds the full output: image.gds, image.bmp, appearance.png, appearance.npz, manifest.json and summary.json. The NPZ stores per-cell reflection spectra and the pixel-to-cell mapping.

Close-up of the polygons read back from the GDS.

What the closed loop covers

The candidate-cell GDS is read back to compute the palette, and the image is mapped onto it. Line widths of frequently used candidates are searched ±1 grid step, then the final GDS is read back and recomputed to match the prediction made during optimization. This checks consistency within one forward model; it is not a calibration against measurements.

Supported are planar stacks where all patterned films share one 1D rectangular line grating. The SKY130 polyimide optical constants and the TiN cap are assumptions. The SOI stack (Al 100 nm / Si 220 nm / BOX 2 µm) is a comparison setting. Arbitrary 2D shapes, independent multi-layer patterns, coupling between neighboring pixels and dummy fill are out of scope.
